Taylor — thanks for the clear notes and the workbook. We're aligned that phased activation is common and we can structure the reserved capacity agreement to support staged activation without change to the committed SKU mix, provided the activation schedule is documented in the SOW.

Options to address GPU price volatility (short summary so we can pick a path):

- Option A — Fixed effective rate with capped exposure: Redwood guarantees the committed unit price for the first 12 months. If NVIDIA spot/market unit cost rises >15% vs baseline, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 50% of the incremental cost for the next quarter. (Requires Sales + Finance sign-off.)

- Option B — Indexation + floor: Contract ties unit cost to a GPU index (monthly). If index rises, customer receives credits when price exceeds a 20% threshold; if index falls, price follows index down (pro-ration). This is more transparent but operationally more complex. (Legal/Finance review needed.)

- Option C — Contingent discount ladder: We commit to standard pricing with a contingency ladder: 0-10% market change = no adjustment; 10-25% = 7.5% customer credit; >25% = up to 15% credit subject to exec approval. This gives a deterministic rebate schedule.

Recommended path for Echelon (because you need predictable budgeting and phased activation): propose Option C as the baseline with a detailed activation phasing schedule in the SOW; include a clause to revisit after 12 months if market volatility persists.

Action items: 
- Taylor / Procurement: confirm preferred phasing dates and whether you want credits applied monthly or as quarter lumps.
- Kimberly / Finance: can you confirm if Option C fits within discount authority or if this requires VP-level approval?
- Sean: any operational constraints on supporting a phased activation tied to a contingency ladder?

I'll assemble a draft SOW language for the phasing and the contingency ladder once we have answers.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Soojin / Sean — quick read and finance/legal perspective: 

- Option C (contingent discount ladder) is the most sales-friendly and easiest to operationalize. It keeps billing simple and sets clear expectations.
- Anything that ties to an external index (Option B) triggers additional monthly billing reconciliation and needs approvals from Finance Ops; we should avoid unless the customer insists.
- The one-time credit in Option A is OK but less predictable for customers and internal accruals.

Approval authorities: 
- Up to 10% effective discount can be approved by Sales Ops (documented).
- 10-15% requires VP Sales sign-off. Anything >15% needs CRO/Finance Exec approval.

Suggested language for SOW (short): 
"If Redwood's underlying GPU procurement costs increase by more than 25% relative to the baseline established at contract execution, Redwood will apply a customer credit equal to 15% of incremental token servicing cost for the subsequent quarter, subject to executive approval. For changes between 10% and 25%, Redwood will apply a 7.5% credit automatically."

Operational notes: we should document the baseline (date + SKU mix) and tie credit calculations to usage (not committed units) to prevent gaming. Also include a 12-month review window.

I can draft the clause and send to Legal for insertion into the SOW/MAAP.

-Kim
